subject.title: Device tokens: reduce OAuth credential retention and membership-check amplification

question: After device pairing is accepted, should device credentials retain a sealed owner OAuth grant for their full lifetime, use a short fail-closed membership cache, or require periodic owner reauthorization instead?
rationale: The correct retention and caching policy sets the revocation window, OAuth credential blast radius, rate-limit behavior, and paired-device recovery contract; those are security-boundary choices rather than a mechanical patch decision.

options.title: Define a short-lived revalidation model
options.body: Require short-lived revalidation material or periodic owner reauthorization, cache successful membership checks only briefly while failing closed, and return a distinct reauthorization error when renewal is needed.

options.title: Keep per-request revalidation
options.body: Preserve the strongest immediate revocation behavior and accept GitHub API amplification until real device traffic demonstrates a need for caching.

options.title: Defer pairing rollout
options.body: Pause broader device-client rollout until the credential-retention and revocation model has an approved security design.

recommendation.title: Define a short-lived revalidation model
recommendation.body: Require short-lived revalidation material or periodic owner reauthorization, cache successful membership checks only briefly while failing closed, and return a distinct reauthorization error when renewal is needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The related implementation and this focused follow-up both originate from the same device-pairing security design work.
